Multiple checks were performed over the course of the study denoted by color. 23 4.2 Laser Flash Analysis Four specimens of varying composition were prepared for thermal diffusivity measurements. Each specimen was (wire electrical discharge machined) to have diameters of 12.68 mm±0.01 mm with thicknesses of 1.98 mm±0.005 mm. Thickness and diameter measurements were determined using a Mitutoyo micrometer with an absolute resolution of 0.001 mm. Thickness determination was evaluated on each specimen along the quadrant as well as the center for both faces, a total of 10 measurements, which were averaged to determine the thickness for each specimen. Diametral measurements were determined at 3 different locations and averaged together. Thermal diffusivity measurements were performed in a Netzsch LFA467 HyperFlash unit (LFA) using two samples at a time. Each measurement was performed under an ulta high purity Ar gas environment, which was purged three times with at least one high vacuum step to 1.4E-4 mbar. Temperature calibrations within the LFA were performed using Curie magnetic transitions for Ni, Fe, and Co. Thermal diffusivity was collected on heating and cooling using 50 K intervals to a maximum temperature of 1273 K. Calculation of the thermal heat rise was performed in the Netzsch Proteus 7.0 software package using a Cape-Lehman fitting procedure. Three data points were determined at each temperature increment for statistical averaging, which accounts for a maximum relative diffusivity error of 0.2% at each temperature data point. 5 Samples and Preparation 5.1 Alloying All sample buttons were alloyed from pure components using a non-consumable arc melter (button melter) in an inert atmosphere using Mo (99.99% purity) and uranium (99.95% purity). The Sigma foundry maintains general procedures for depleted uranium alloy melting guidelines, the most relevant for this work being (Non-Consumable Arc-Melting of DU Alloy Buttons, Rev 002, dated 01/05/2021). Existing buttons made in 2013 followed the same general guidelines, though a documented work instruction was not required at that time. It should be noted that the current work instructions were based upon the standard practice at that time. In general, the chamber is pumped down to <50 mTorr, isolated to measure leak rate, then pumped down again prior to inert backfill. The inert gas is a Ar-15%He mixture at a pressure of -10 inHg (or ~400 Torr), and prior to melting the alloys, a pure zirconium button is melted for ~1 minute in order to scavenge stray oxygen.
